title: Texas franchise tax forfeiture: losing the right to transact business
rule: If a taxable entity does not file a required franchise tax report, including the Public Information Report, or does not pay a tax or penalty, the Comptroller sends notice and, if the failure is not cured within 45 days, forfeits the entity's right to transact business without a court proceeding. A forfeited entity cannot sue or defend in a Texas court, and its officers and directors become liable for its debts incurred in Texas after the report or tax was due and before revival. Filing and paying what is due revives the right. If it is not revived within 120 days, the Secretary of State may forfeit the entity's registration.
changeWatch: Amendments to Tax Code chapter 171, subchapters F and G; section 171.251 was last amended effective September 1, 2023.
